title: Binary Search Trees: Search
oneLiner: The same left/right comparison as Insert, but stop and report found instead of placing a new node.
keyTakeaway: Searching a BST is Insert's comparison logic with the ending changed: instead of placing a new node when you fall off the tree, falling off means the value isn't there. Same walk, same O(h) cost (h = tree height -- O(log n) if balanced, O(n) if it's degenerated into a linked-list shape).
explanation: Start at the root and compare: found it, exact match -- done, return true. Target is smaller -- it can ONLY be in the left subtree (everything in the right subtree is guaranteed bigger or equal by the BST invariant, so bigger than the target), so move left and repeat. Target is bigger -- move right for the same reason. If this walk ever reaches an empty spot (null) before finding a match, the value isn't in the tree at all -- there's nowhere else it could be. This lesson gives you `BuildBst` (the same insertion helper from the previous lesson) already implemented, so you can focus purely on the search logic itself. Watch out for the direction mix-up: smaller means left, not right -- easy to get backward under time pressure, and a backward search will silently return wrong answers (false negatives) instead of crashing, which makes the bug harder to notice.

visualizationSteps.message: Searching for 7. Start at the root.

complexity.note: SearchBst first builds the tree from the n values with the given helper: n inserts at up to h steps each, O(n · h), which is O(n log n) balanced and O(n²) for sorted input. That build dominates. The search itself, the part this lesson is about, is one root-to-leaf walk: O(h), which is O(log n) balanced and O(n) degenerate, with O(1) extra space for the iterative loop. The tree takes O(n) space.
